claims.note: Tours read at origin/fix/tour-6-format-check (PR 40). I reproduced the 2,000-try figure myself instead of taking the relayed number. Probe: a console program against NetSec.Core at origin/main (aff0619) builds a real PIN block for KSN counter 1, flips bytes in it 2,000 times, and calls DukptBank.OpenPinSale each time on one ledger. Output: 'forged tries=2000 ksnFreeAfterEach=2000 lastCode=DUKPT_PINBLOCK_FORMAT' then 'real sale code=null pin=1234'. So the format check refuses every forged block, never records the KSN, and has no try limit; the real sale still passes afterwards. Code: DukptBank.OpenPinSale records the KSN only when sale.Code is null. PR 35 body, table row 'A forged block burns a real sale's KSN' and advisory 3 ('The format check is not integrity') agree. CMAC half: BankHsmCore.Decide (src/NetSec.Core/Bridge/PinEnvelope.cs) derives the MAC key from the BDK and KSN and verifies the CMAC before it checks the ledger, so a block from someone without the key is refused before the format check. program-design.md section 6, PIN-pad row, names the PinEnvelope with a MAC. Limits: the word 'lesson 9' is a plan statement. Lesson 9 has no tour yet, and the bridge acceptance clauses that need the server role report NODE_ROLE_NOT_BUILT in PR 35. The code facts hold today; the end-to-end lesson does not exist yet. Suggest replacing the relayed 2,000 figure in the source line with the probe command and output, since the claim then rests on a run rather than a message.

problems.wrong: The reader holds a starting key of its own, made from the BDK and the reader's id. ... Each side derives it.
problems.right: The reader holds a starting key of its own. In this lab the setup derives it from the BDK and the reader's id and loads it into the reader, like a key put in at a secure facility. The bank derives the same key. The key never crosses the wire.
problems.evidence: Lesson06Dukpt.cs: LoadReader(DukptBank.DeriveInitialKey(bdk, InitialKeyId)). Step S02 says the reader never gets a copy of the BDK, so the reader cannot derive it.
